# Code of Conduct

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant v2.0 and modified to
reflect the scale and operating model of this project.

---

## Purpose

The purpose of this document is to establish a minimum set of rules that allow
technical discussions and contributions to happen without personal attacks,
unproductive arguments, or maintainer burnout.

This document:
- Is not a declaration intended to eliminate all technical disagreements.
- Does not aim to protect all opinions equally.
- Firmly blocks behaviors where attacks on people undermine technical discussion.

---

## Our Pledge

All participants in this project (users, contributors, reviewers, and maintainers)
commit to:
- Maintaining an environment where individuals are treated with dignity regardless of background, level of experience, or identity.
- Welcoming robust, rigorous criticism of code and architectural design, while strictly prohibiting personal attacks.
- Framing discussions around solving real engineering problems, not "winning" arguments.

---

## Expected Behavior

- Discussions and critiques based strictly on technical reasoning and architectural merits.
- Respect for peers who propose different technical trade-offs.
- Acknowledging mistakes gracefully and correcting them promptly.
- Filing bug reports and pull requests with clear context, logs, and reproducible steps.
- Respecting the time and energy of the maintainer.

---

## Unacceptable Behavior

The following behaviors are strictly prohibited:
- Insults, mockery, ad hominem attacks, or demeaning language.
- Harassment, sexualized language, hate speech, or personal threats.
- Deliberate trolling, inflammatory remarks, or bad-faith disruption of issues/PRs.
- Publishing private communications or personal data without consent.
- Entitled attitudes demanding immediate assistance, custom feature development, or 24/7 support.

**In particular:** Open source software is provided in good faith. The assumption that maintainers owe free, immediate consulting or custom labor is fundamentally rejected in this project.

---

## Communication Guidelines

- Keep issues and pull requests focused on the repository's concrete scope.
- Bug reports must include minimal, reproducible examples.
- Do not hijack existing issues with unrelated discussions or feature requests.
- Low-effort or spam requests may be closed without extensive debate.

Maintainers have professional and personal lives outside this repository; please communicate with patience and professional courtesy.

---

## Enforcement

Project maintainers reserve the right to edit, close, or delete any issue, pull request, or comment that violates this Code of Conduct, and to temporarily or permanently ban any contributor exhibiting disruptive or abusive behavior.
